description: Interactive drag-and-drop sorting tool for classifying questions as Statistical or Non-Statistical. Students read question cards and drag them into the correct bin. Includes hints on wrong answers, animated feedback, confetti celebration, and a full results summary with explanations. Designed for Grade 7 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Connecting the Dots.

themeColor.description: Primary theme color (hex) — Singularity design system purple

additionalProps.description: Tool-specific dynamic content passed by the agent to customize questions, title, and subtitle

id.description: Unique numeric ID for the question

text.description: The question text displayed on the card

isStatistical.description: true if the question is statistical, false if non-statistical

explanation.description: Explanation shown in the results summary for why this question is or isn't statistical

hint.description: Hint shown when the student drags the card to the wrong bin

icon.description: Emoji icon displayed on the card (e.g. '📏', '🕷️', '🏏')

questions.description: Array of question cards. If null, uses 8 built-in default questions covering Grade 7 topics.

title.description: Main heading displayed in the header

subtitle.default: Chapter 5: Connecting the Dots — Grade 7 Mathematics
subtitle.description: Subtitle/chapter reference shown below the badge

default_questions.title: Statistical vs Non-Statistical Questions
default_questions.subtitle: Chapter 5: Connecting the Dots — Grade 7 Mathematics

questions.text: How many pets do students in our class have?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Different students have different numbers of pets — there is variability.
questions.hint: Would every student give the same answer?

questions.text: How many days are in a week?
questions.explanation: Not statistical — there are always exactly 7 days in a week. No variability.
questions.hint: Is the answer always the same?

questions.text: What is the favourite ice cream flavour of students in Grade 7?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Different students have different preferences. You need to survey to find out.
questions.hint: Does everyone like the same flavour?

questions.text: What is the boiling point of water?
questions.explanation: Not statistical — water always boils at 100°C at standard pressure. Fixed answer.
questions.hint: Does this change depending on who you ask?

questions.text: What are the prices of tomatoes at different shops today?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Prices vary from shop to shop.
questions.hint: Would every shop charge the same?

questions.text: How many grams are in one kilogram?
questions.explanation: Not statistical — always 1000 grams. Fixed fact.

questions.text: How many customers visit the mandi each hour?
questions.explanation: Statistical! The count changes every hour — variability exists.
questions.hint: Is it the same number every hour?

questions.text: Which vegetables are most popular among families in our area?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Different families prefer different vegetables.
questions.hint: Does every family buy the same vegetables?

questions.text: What is the Hindi word for potato?
questions.explanation: Not statistical — it's always 'aloo'. Fixed fact with no variability.

questions.text: How much weight of vegetables do different shops sell in a day?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Each shop sells different amounts — you need data to find out.
questions.hint: Do all shops sell the same amount?

questions.text: How many runs did each player score in yesterday's cricket match?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Each player scored differently — classic variability.
questions.hint: Did every player score the same runs?

questions.text: How many players are in a football team on the field?
questions.explanation: Not statistical — always 11 players. Fixed rule.

questions.text: What are the heights of basketball players in the NBA?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Players have different heights — you need to measure many players.
questions.hint: Are all basketball players the same height?

questions.text: How many sets are needed to win a tennis match in a Grand Slam (men's)?
questions.explanation: Not statistical — you always need 3 sets (best of 5). Fixed rule.
questions.hint: Is this a rule that changes?

questions.text: How much time do students in our school spend playing sports each week?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Different students spend different amounts of time. Variability!
questions.hint: Does every student play the same number of hours?

questions.text: Which sport is most popular among students in Class 7?
questions.explanation: Statistical! Preferences vary — you'd need to survey the class.
questions.hint: Would you need to ask multiple students?

questions.text: How old are the students in your class?

questions.explanation: Not statistical — the answer is always 3.

sort.description: Single interactive mode — students drag question cards into Statistical or Non-Statistical bins

features.drag_and_drop: Cards can be dragged (mouse and touch) into two sorting bins
features.wrong_answer_feedback: Cards shake and return to the unsorted pile with a hint displayed
features.correct_answer_feedback: Cards celebrate with animation and move into the bin permanently
features.progress_bar: Header shows a live progress bar of correctly sorted cards
features.confetti: Confetti animation plays when all cards are correctly sorted
features.results_summary: Expandable table showing all questions, their categories, and explanations
features.key_takeaway: Summary includes a 'Key Pattern to Remember' section
features.teacher_prompt: Summary includes a prompt asking students to create their own questions
features.reset_shuffle: Reset button shuffles cards and starts over
